_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

pivotal_trials.design: 64-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis eligible for systemic therapy or phototherapy (PGA ≥3, PASI ≥12, BSA ≥10%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: proportion achieving PGA 0/1 ("cleared"/"minimal") and proportion achieving PASI 75
pivotal_trials.n: N=309 ILUMYA 100 mg; N=154 placebo (Trial 2/P010 arms)
pivotal_trials.result: Trial P010 at Week 12: PGA 0/1 58% vs 7% placebo; PASI 75 64% vs 6% placebo (p-values <0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind double-dummy, placebo- and active-comparator (etanercept 50 mg)-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis eligible for systemic therapy or phototherapy (PGA ≥3, PASI ≥12, BSA ≥10%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: proportion achieving PGA 0/1 ("cleared"/"minimal") and proportion achieving PASI 75
pivotal_trials.n: N=307 ILUMYA 100 mg; N=156 placebo (Trial 3/P011 arms)
pivotal_trials.result: Trial P011 at Week 12: PGA 0/1 55% vs 4% placebo; PASI 75 61% vs 6% placebo (p-values <0.001)

key_safety: Most common (≥1%) adverse reactions are upper respiratory infections (14% vs 12% placebo), injection site reactions (3% vs 2%), and diarrhea (2% vs 1%). Infections occurred in 23% of ILUMYA subjects. Serious risks include hypersensitivity reactions and infections.
target_moa: Humanized IgG1/κ monoclonal antibody that specifically binds the p19 subunit of IL-23 and inhibits its interaction with the IL-23 receptor; an interleukin-23 antagonist

rems.type: No REMS required; risk mitigation beyond professional labeling and a Medication Guide is not required

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held for this application

description.text: Added information about the treatment of adult patients with moderate to severe psoriasis of the scalp

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for changes to the Prescribing Information to add information about the treatment of adult patients with moderate to severe psoriasis of the scalp.

description.text: Updated Section 14 with clinical trial data in subjects with scalp psoriasis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for updates to Section 14 of the USPI with data from a clinical trial in subjects with psoriasis of the scalp.

description.text: Added data supporting treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis patients who also have moderate to severe nail psoriasis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides efficacy and safety data for tildrakizumab-asmn for the treatment of adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy and who also have moderate to severe psoriasis of the nails.

summary.text: ILUMYA was an original BLA under section 351(a) of the PHS Act, given standard review, and approved on the basis of two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (P010 and P011) without accelerated approval or special designations.

citations.quote: Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. submitted a Biologics License Application (BLA) dated March 23, 2017 under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for ILUMYA (tildrakizumab-asmn) injection, for subcutaneous use.

The applicant submitted data from two adequate and well-controlled trials (Trial P010 and Trial P011), which provided evidence of the effectiveness of tildrakizumab for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

requirement.text: 3357-1: Conduct a PK, safety and efficacy study in pediatric subjects 6 to 17 years of age with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (deferred pediatric study under PREA)

citations.quote: 3357-1 Conduct a pharmacokinetics (PK), safety and efficacy study in pediatric subjects 6 years to 17 years of age with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (with a duration of exposure to tildrakizumab-asmn of at least one year).

requirement.text: 3357-2: A prospective, registry-based observational exposure cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to tildrakizumab-asmn during pregnancy versus an unexposed control population

citations.quote: 3357-2 A prospective, registry-based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to tildrakizumab-asmn during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3357-3: A retrospective cohort or case control study to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, neonatal deaths, and infant infections in women exposed to tildrakizumab-asmn during pregnancy

citations.quote: 3357-3 Conduct a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, neonatal deaths, and infant infections in women exposed to tildrakizumab-asmn during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3357-4: An observational study to assess long-term safety of tildrakizumab-asmn compared to other therapies, with primary outcome long-term risk of malignancy

citations.quote: 3357-4 Conduct an observational study to assess the long-term safety of tildrakizumab-asmn compared to other therapies used in the treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy in the course of actual clinical care. The study's primary outcome is the long-term risk of malignancy.
